title: Ballad of the Open Road
technique: Left hand strides between a low bass note and mid-range chords on the off-beats. Keep the tempo relaxed and the melody singing; accuracy matters more than speed.
body: Ballad of the Open Road is a complete jazz piano song in Eb major, in 4/4 time at 64 beats per minute, running 32 bars in A-A-B-A form across 4 sections. Its mood is swing feel and extended harmony over walking or striding bass. The A sections move through ii-V-I-vi turnaround, while the contrasting section changes the harmonic color before the form returns home. This is a Signature-original composition, written new in the genre's language. It is not a copy of any existing song and it is not attributed to any composer outside the Signature system. To play it, keep the left hand steady and unhurried while the right hand sings above it: striding bass and chords in the left hand Practice it first hands separately, then together at half tempo, and only then at full tempo, listening for clean releases between chords so no harmony blurs into the next.

title: Blue Lamp Ballad
technique: Left hand walks the bass in steady quarter notes through the chord tones. Keep the tempo relaxed and the melody singing; accuracy matters more than speed.
body: Blue Lamp Ballad is a complete jazz piano song in C major, in 4/4 time at 132 beats per minute, running 32 bars in A-A-B-A form across 4 sections. Its mood is swing feel and extended harmony over walking or striding bass. The A sections move through ii-V-I-vi turnaround, while the contrasting section changes the harmonic color before the form returns home. This is a Signature-original composition, written new in the genre's language. It is not a copy of any existing song and it is not attributed to any composer outside the Signature system. To play it, keep the left hand steady and unhurried while the right hand sings above it: walking bass in the left hand Practice it first hands separately, then together at half tempo, and only then at full tempo, listening for clean releases between chords so no harmony blurs into the next.

title: The All-Night Diner Swing
technique: Left hand strides between a low bass note and mid-range chords on the off-beats. Shape the phrasing in two-bar breaths and let the syncopation sit inside the beat, never ahead of it.
body: The All-Night Diner Swing is a complete jazz piano song in G major, in 4/4 time at 64 beats per minute, running 32 bars in A-A-B-A form across 4 sections. Its mood is swing feel and extended harmony over walking or striding bass. The A sections move through ii-V-I-vi turnaround, while the contrasting section changes the harmonic color before the form returns home. This is a Signature-original composition, written new in the genre's language. It is not a copy of any existing song and it is not attributed to any composer outside the Signature system. To play it, keep the left hand steady and unhurried while the right hand sings above it: striding bass and chords in the left hand Practice it first hands separately, then together at half tempo, and only then at full tempo, listening for clean releases between chords so no harmony blurs into the next.

title: Blues for the Long Commute
technique: Left hand plays a low bass note answered by mid-range chord blocks. Shape the phrasing in two-bar breaths and let the syncopation sit inside the beat, never ahead of it.
body: Blues for the Long Commute is a complete jazz piano song in F major, in 4/4 time at 176 beats per minute, running 32 bars in A-B-A-B form across 4 sections. Its mood is swing feel and extended harmony over walking or striding bass. The A sections move through ii-V-I-vi turnaround, while the contrasting section changes the harmonic color before the form returns home. This is a Signature-original composition, written new in the genre's language. It is not a copy of any existing song and it is not attributed to any composer outside the Signature system. To play it, keep the left hand steady and unhurried while the right hand sings above it: bass note plus chord blocks in the left hand Practice it first hands separately, then together at half tempo, and only then at full tempo, listening for clean releases between chords so no harmony blurs into the next.

title: The Lamplight Ballad
technique: Left hand strides between a low bass note and mid-range chords on the off-beats. Shape the phrasing in two-bar breaths and let the syncopation sit inside the beat, never ahead of it.
body: The Lamplight Ballad is a complete jazz piano song in Eb major, in 4/4 time at 64 beats per minute, running 32 bars in A-A-B-A form across 4 sections. Its mood is swing feel and extended harmony over walking or striding bass. The A sections move through ii-V-I-vi turnaround, while the contrasting section changes the harmonic color before the form returns home. This is a Signature-original composition, written new in the genre's language. It is not a copy of any existing song and it is not attributed to any composer outside the Signature system. To play it, keep the left hand steady and unhurried while the right hand sings above it: striding bass and chords in the left hand Practice it first hands separately, then together at half tempo, and only then at full tempo, listening for clean releases between chords so no harmony blurs into the next.

title: Swing Down Riverside Drive
technique: Left hand plays a low bass note answered by mid-range chord blocks. At full tempo the passagework must stay even and light; practice the fastest bars slowly until every note speaks.
body: Swing Down Riverside Drive is a complete jazz piano song in A major, in 4/4 time at 176 beats per minute, running 32 bars in A-B-A-B form across 4 sections. Its mood is swing feel and extended harmony over walking or striding bass. The A sections move through ii-V-I-vi turnaround, while the contrasting section changes the harmonic color before the form returns home. This is a Signature-original composition, written new in the genre's language. It is not a copy of any existing song and it is not attributed to any composer outside the Signature system. To play it, keep the left hand steady and unhurried while the right hand sings above it: bass note plus chord blocks in the left hand Practice it first hands separately, then together at half tempo, and only then at full tempo, listening for clean releases between chords so no harmony blurs into the next.

Its mood is swing feel and extended harmony over walking or striding bass. The A sections move through ii-V-I-vi turnaround, while the contrasting section changes the harmonic color before the form returns home. This is a Signature-original composition, written new in the genre's language. It is not a copy of any existing song and it is not attributed to any composer outside the Signature system. To play it, keep the left hand steady and unhurried while the right hand sings above it: walking bass in the left hand Practice it first hands separately, then together at half tempo, and only then at full tempo, listening for clean releases between chords so no harmony blurs into the next.

title: Stride in the Morning Light
technique: Left hand walks the bass in steady quarter notes through the chord tones. At full tempo the passagework must stay even and light; practice the fastest bars slowly until every note speaks.
body: Stride in the Morning Light is a complete jazz piano song in C major, in 4/4 time at 132 beats per minute, running 32 bars in A-A-B-A form across 4 sections. Its mood is swing feel and extended harmony over walking or striding bass. The A sections move through ii-V-I-vi turnaround, while the contrasting section changes the harmonic color before the form returns home. This is a Signature-original composition, written new in the genre's language. It is not a copy of any existing song and it is not attributed to any composer outside the Signature system. To play it, keep the left hand steady and unhurried while the right hand sings above it: walking bass in the left hand Practice it first hands separately, then together at half tempo, and only then at full tempo, listening for clean releases between chords so no harmony blurs into the next.

title: The Bebop Bookshop
technique: Left hand strides between a low bass note and mid-range chords on the off-beats. At full tempo the passagework must stay even and light; practice the fastest bars slowly until every note speaks.
body: The Bebop Bookshop is a complete jazz piano song in G major, in 4/4 time at 64 beats per minute, running 32 bars in A-A-B-A form across 4 sections. Its mood is swing feel and extended harmony over walking or striding bass. The A sections move through twelve-bar blues roots in eight-bar sections, while the contrasting section changes the harmonic color before the form returns home. This is a Signature-original composition, written new in the genre's language. It is not a copy of any existing song and it is not attributed to any composer outside the Signature system. To play it, keep the left hand steady and unhurried while the right hand sings above it: striding bass and chords in the left hand Practice it first hands separately, then together at half tempo, and only then at full tempo, listening for clean releases between chords so no harmony blurs into the next.

technique: Left hand plays a low bass note answered by mid-range chord blocks. At full tempo the passagework must stay even and light; practice the fastest bars slowly until every note speaks.
body: Last Set at the Corner Club is a complete jazz piano song in F major, in 4/4 time at 176 beats per minute, running 32 bars in A-B-A-B form across 4 sections. Its mood is swing feel and extended harmony over walking or striding bass. The A sections move through ii-V-I-vi turnaround, while the contrasting section changes the harmonic color before the form returns home. This is a Signature-original composition, written new in the genre's language. It is not a copy of any existing song and it is not attributed to any composer outside the Signature system. To play it, keep the left hand steady and unhurried while the right hand sings above it: bass note plus chord blocks in the left hand Practice it first hands separately, then together at half tempo, and only then at full tempo, listening for clean releases between chords so no harmony blurs into the next.
